title: A docs answerer with citations and a refusal test set
summary: Build a question-answering tool over a product's documentation that cites its sources, refuses what the docs do not say, and proves both with a test set.
context: Quillstack is a fictional developer-tools company that wants a help box answering from its docs and never from guesswork. Support teams care less about clever answers than about wrong ones, and about which page an answer came from.
You write the docs: about 25 short Markdown pages for an invented product, such as a fictional queue-monitoring API. Let one page contradict an older one on purpose and leave some obvious gaps.
Then build retrieval and answering. Every answer cites the passage it relies on; a question the docs do not answer gets a refusal that says what the docs do cover.
must_have: The invented docs corpus in the repo, chunked and indexed by a method you chose and can explain.
An answer function returning the answer plus, for each claim, the chunk it came from, with page and heading.

A test set of 40 questions: 25 the docs answer (with the expected page), 10 they do not (refusal expected), and 5 tricky ones, such as a superseded page or a question that sounds answerable but is not.
An evaluation script reporting retrieval hit rate, citation correctness, refusal precision and recall, and listing every failure.
A code check that an answer cannot cite a chunk that was not retrieved, with a test.
nice_to_have: Two chunking or retrieval settings compared on the same test set.
Preferring the newer page when two disagree, and saying so in the answer.
A page in the corpus that contains instructions aimed at the model, and what your system does with it.
constraints: No paid services, APIs or accounts. Use a local model or a free tier with no card, and commit recorded outputs so the evaluation reproduces without a key.
Fictional product, docs and company only. Do not copy real documentation.
deliverables: A public repo created after you press Start, with commits spread across the window.
A README with how to run it (build the index, ask a question, run the evaluation), your scores, and what is missing.
judge_focus: How the refusal threshold was chosen and what it cost in answers lost.
Whether citations are verified in code or merely requested from a model.
Whether the test set could have failed your system, and whether the commit history shows it written before you tuned.
Your account of what AI produced, what you verified, and what you threw away.
bengaluru_context: Developer-experience, support-tooling and AI product teams at Bengaluru software companies are building this feature now, and the interview question is always how you stop it making things up.
